slides.title: A mock customer: Acme Corp
slides.lede: A rebrand, a rule-gated navigation entry, and a custom panel — with zero edits to our libraries. Everything after this slide is running code.

items.title: Our brand, not yours
items.text: "Acme Content" in the header and the browser tab, and our navy in the navigation. **Layer 0** — a bootstrap fragment and a reload.

items.title: A section only our legal team sees
items.text: A navigation entry gated on a rule we write ourselves, against our own notion of who is signed in. **Layer 2**.

items.title: A panel that is ours, placed by configuration
items.text: A component we own, contributed by ID, so it can be routed or dropped into a drawer without anyone importing our class. **Layer 2 + Layer 1**.

items.title: And we will not fork the platform
items.text: Because next quarter we want to take your upgrade as a version bump.

slides.title: The rebrand is a JSON fragment
slides.lede: No rebuild, no redeploy of the application bundle. A bootstrap fragment in Acme's own configuration package, reload, done — and it survives the next marketplace upgrade because that package is theirs, not part of ours.

blocks.code: // Acme's bootstrap fragment, in their configuration package { "branding": { "applicationTitle": "Acme Content", "documentTitle": "Acme Content" }, "defaultThemeId": "acme", "themes": [{ "id": "acme", "label": "Acme", "base": "nuxeo", "tokens": { "--shell-nav-bg": "#0f2b46", // Acme navy "--shell-nav-fg": "#eef4fb", "--shell-nav-active": "#1f6feb" } }] }

slides.footnote: The nav carries its own foreground token deliberately. Without it, a customer darkening the navigation background would render dark text on a dark background — a rebrand must not be able to make navigation unreadable from JSON alone. The Phase 4 evidence asserts a luminance gap after the rebrand.

slides.title: One command scaffolds the library

blocks.code: $ npx nx g @nuxeo-satori/generators:extension-library acme-extensions --owner=acme CREATE libs/extensions/acme-extensions/src/lib/extensions.ts CREATE libs/extensions/acme-extensions/src/lib/extensions.spec.ts 6 specs CREATE libs/extensions/acme-extensions/src/lib/rules.service.ts CREATE libs/extensions/acme-extensions/src/lib/panel/acme-panel.ts CREATE libs/extensions/acme-extensions/README.md UPDATE tsconfig.base.json import alias It is inert until an application opts in. Add one line: import { provideAcmeExtensions } from '@agentic-ui/acme-extensions'; // providers: [ ..., provideAcmeExtensions() ]

slides.footnote: Fourteen files, including a `test`, `lint` and `typecheck` target. The six generated specs assert against the **registries**, not that a function was called — because "the ID is registered" is the only thing that catches a descriptor nothing renders.

slides.title: What Acme actually writes

blocks.code: // libs/extensions/acme-extensions/src/lib/extensions.ts export const ACME_EXTENSIONS_EXTENSION_IDS = Object.freeze({ navbar: ['acme.navbar.acmeExtensions'], rules: ['acme.rules.canUseAcme'], actions: ['acme.actions.acmeExtensionsExport'], components: ['acme.panel.acmeExtensions'], }); export function provideAcmeExtensions(): EnvironmentProviders { return provideSatoriExtensions(() => { const rules = inject(AcmeRulesService); return { slots: { navbar: NAV_ITEMS }, rules: { 'acme.rules.canUseAcme': (ctx) => rules.canUse(ctx) }, failClosedRules: ['acme.rules.canUseAcme'], components: { 'acme.panel.acmeExtensions': () => import('./panel/acme-panel')... }, actions: { 'acme.actions.acmeExtensionsExport': { execute: ... } }, }; }); }

slides.footnote: The library exports **only** the provider and the ID list. Deliberately: a host that could import the panel class would depend on a name that should stay free to change. The host maps a path; `ExtensionOutletComponent` resolves the component from the registry by ID.

slides.title: And then configuration moves it, without touching the library
slides.lede: The same IDs Acme registered in code are now addressable from the manifest — by their own administrators, with no developer involved.

blocks.code: // Acme's manifest fragment, in their configuration package — no rebuild { "extensions": { "overrides": { // Rename Acme's own entry and move it to the top "acme.navbar.acmeExtensions": { "label": "Contracts", "order": 5 } }, "slots": { // Or place Acme's panel in a drawer instead of on a route "sidebar": [{ "id": "acme.sidebar.contracts", "label": "Contracts", "component": "acme.panel.acmeExtensions", "order": 10 }] } } }

slides.footnote: This is the payoff of IDs being the contract. The code says *what exists*; configuration says *where it appears and when* — and the two can be changed by different people, at different times, with different permissions.

slides.title: Zero edits to our libraries
slides.lede: Not asserted — read out of `git status` after integrating the generated library into the template.

blocks.code: $ git status --short M apps/nuxeo-satori-template/src/app/app.config.ts one line + one import M tsconfig.base.json one alias, written by the generator ?? libs/extensions/acme-extensions/ Acme's own library $ git status --short | grep -E 'libs/shared/|libs/platform/' (no output — no platform library was modified)

slides.footnote: Verified again by the Phase 4 evidence run, which clicks Acme's navigation entry in a browser and asserts both the URL and the panel's own markup — because a wildcard redirect back to the home page would still leave a rendered page and a green-looking check.

slides.title: A rebrand, a gated entry and a custom panel — none of it a fork

blocks.text: Acme changed the brand from a bootstrap fragment, added a rule-gated section and a panel from their own npm library, and their administrators can still move both from the manifest. Our libraries are byte-for-byte unchanged, so next quarter's upgrade is a version bump.

slides.footnote: Still honest about what is not proven: the platform has never been published to a registry, and no test resolves its ten peer dependencies from a clean install. The first real publish will be tagged `alpha` for exactly that reason.
